sub_graphs.title: EIP-712: Typed Data Signing Lifecycle
sub_graphs.description: Models the lifecycle of signing typed structured data via eth_signTypedData

nodes.label: Sign Request Received
nodes.description: Wallet receives eth_signTypedData request with typed data JSON

nodes.label: Parse Typed Data JSON
nodes.description: Extract types, primaryType, domain, and message from JSON payload

nodes.label: Typed Data Parsed
nodes.description: Typed data structure successfully parsed and validated

nodes.label: Validate Account Address
nodes.description: Verify the 20-byte address parameter and check account status

nodes.label: Account Locked
nodes.description: Requested account is locked, cannot sign

nodes.label: Account Unlocked
nodes.description: Account is unlocked and ready to sign

nodes.label: Display Data to User
nodes.description: Present human-readable representation of structured data for user approval

nodes.label: Awaiting User Approval
nodes.description: Wallet UI showing data, waiting for user to approve or reject

nodes.label: User Rejected Signing
nodes.description: User declined to sign the message

nodes.label: User Approved Signing
nodes.description: User confirmed they want to sign the message

nodes.label: Compute Signable Hash
nodes.description: Compute the final hash: keccak256(0x1901 || domainSeparator || hashStruct(message))

nodes.label: Hash Computed
nodes.description: 32-byte signable hash is ready

nodes.label: Sign Hash with Private Key
nodes.description: Apply ECDSA signature using account's private key

nodes.label: Signature Ready
nodes.description: 65-byte signature (r, s, v) is computed and returned

external_entities.name: Decentralized Application
external_entities.description: Web application requesting user signature on structured data via wallet

external_entities.name: Wallet User
external_entities.description: Human user who approves or rejects signing requests

sub_graphs.title: EIP-712: Typed Data Encoding and Hashing
sub_graphs.description: Models the encoding rules for typed structured data hashing

nodes.label: Raw Typed Data Received
nodes.description: Typed data object with types, domain, and message fields

nodes.label: Encode Type Definition
nodes.description: Generate type encoding string: 'TypeName(type1 member1,type2 member2,...)'

nodes.label: Type String Encoded
nodes.description: Canonical type encoding string is ready

nodes.label: Compute Type Hash
nodes.description: Calculate keccak256(encodeType(type))

nodes.label: Type Hash Computed
nodes.description: 32-byte typeHash is available

nodes.label: Encode Data Values
nodes.description: Encode each member according to its type (atomic: pad to 32 bytes, dynamic: keccak256)

nodes.label: Data Values Encoded
nodes.description: All member values are encoded as 32-byte chunks

nodes.label: Compute Struct Hash
nodes.description: Calculate hashStruct = keccak256(typeHash || encodeData(s))

nodes.label: Struct Hash Computed
nodes.description: 32-byte hashStruct is ready

nodes.label: Encode Domain Separator
nodes.description: Compute hashStruct(eip712Domain) with name, version, chainId, verifyingContract, salt

nodes.label: Domain Separator Computed
nodes.description: 32-byte domain separator is ready

nodes.label: Compute Final Hash
nodes.description: Calculate keccak256(0x19 || 0x01 || domainSeparator || hashStruct(message))

nodes.label: Final Signable Hash Ready
nodes.description: 32-byte hash ready for ECDSA signing

sub_graphs.title: EIP-712: Security Boundaries and Attack Vectors
sub_graphs.description: Models security considerations including replay protection and domain separation

nodes.label: Valid Signature Created
nodes.description: User has signed a typed data message

nodes.label: Attacker Captures Signature
nodes.description: Malicious actor obtains a valid signature from broadcast or other means

nodes.label: Signature Captured by Attacker
nodes.description: Attacker has the signature and original message

nodes.label: Attempt Signature Replay
nodes.description: Attacker tries to reuse signature for unintended purpose

nodes.label: Replay on Same Domain
nodes.description: Attacker tries to replay on the same contract/chain

nodes.label: Replay on Different Domain
nodes.description: Attacker tries to replay on a different contract or chain

nodes.label: Verify Domain Separator
nodes.description: Verifier checks that domain separator matches expected value

nodes.label: Domain Separator Mismatch
nodes.description: Signature invalid for this domain - cross-domain replay prevented

nodes.label: Domain Separator Matches
nodes.description: Signature is valid for this domain

nodes.label: Check Application-Level Nonce
nodes.description: Application checks if signature has been used before (not part of EIP-712)

nodes.label: Replay Attack Blocked
nodes.description: Application-level protection prevents signature reuse

nodes.label: Replay Attack Succeeded
nodes.description: Application without replay protection accepted duplicate signature

external_entities.name: Malicious Actor
external_entities.description: Attacker attempting to replay or misuse captured signatures

external_entities.name: Verifying Smart Contract
external_entities.description: On-chain contract that verifies EIP-712 signatures

ambiguities.text: The standard 'does not include replay protection' - applications must implement their own, but no standard mechanism is defined.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume applications must include a nonce in their typed data schema and track used nonces. This is a critical security requirement left to implementers.

ambiguities.text: The specification states domain separator fields 'must appear in order' but also says 'user-agents should accept any order'. This is contradictory.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the canonical encoding must use the specified order, but JSON input parsing should be order-agnostic.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'Protocol designers only need to include the fields that make sense for their signing domain' leaves significant discretion without guidance.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume at minimum: name, version, and chainId should be included for any on-chain verification to prevent cross-chain replays.

ambiguities.text: Handling of recursive struct types with circular references is not explicitly addressed.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume circular references are not supported - each struct must be definable with a finite type encoding string.

implicit_assumptions.description: Wallets will faithfully display the typed data to users before signing, without modification or obfuscation.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious or compromised wallets could trick users into signing unintended messages, enabling theft or unauthorized actions.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot construct a different typed data structure that produces the same hash as a legitimate message.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Hash collision would allow signature forgery, completely breaking the security model.

implicit_assumptions.description: The chainId in the domain separator matches the actual chain where the signature will be verified.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Cross-chain replay attacks possible if chainId is omitted or mismatched.

implicit_assumptions.description: Verifying contracts correctly implement the EIP-712 encoding and hashing algorithm.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect implementations could accept invalid signatures or reject valid ones, leading to security vulnerabilities or denial of service.

implicit_assumptions.description: The dApp correctly encodes the typed data structure according to its intended meaning.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious dApps could encode misleading structures where displayed meaning differs from verified meaning.
